parameters.name: Mode
parameters.explanation: The selected mode changes how the support surface inflates or cycles its air cells. Verify the mode against the care plan and device instructions. Continue skin checks and repositioning.

parameters.name: Air level or pressure state
parameters.explanation: An inflation indication describes the support surface state. It does not measure pressure on the patient’s skin. Assess the patient’s position, skin and surface function.

parameters.name: Alarm state
parameters.explanation: A support-surface alarm identifies a device or therapy problem according to its manual. Assess the patient and surface, then follow the model-specific response and arrange alternate support if needed.

safety_concepts.text: Use equipment and low-friction fabrics that reduce friction and shear when moving the patient.

monitoring_concepts.text: Reposition on a schedule set by mobility, skin and tissue tolerance, clinical condition, comfort and the support surface, not a fixed rule.

The guideline notes that critically ill individuals, or others with systemic hypoperfusion or shock states, may need more frequent, incremental repositioning, and may benefit from supplementing full-body repositioning with assisted small shifts in body position.
Assess for early signs of skin and tissue injury, which may mean the individual needs more frequent repositioning or preferential positioning off the damaged area.

escalation_concepts.text: Report new skin changes and device-related damage promptly.
